definitions.gloss: reward money; bonus; bounty; incentive payment
definitions.explanation: Money given as a reward for a specific achievement, contribution, or desired action. Can refer to corporate bonuses, government incentives, or rewards for information.

examples.japanese: {報奨金|ほうしょうきん}が{支払|しはら}われた。
{有力|ゆうりょく}な{情報|じょうほう}を{提供|ていきょう}した{人|ひと}には{報奨金|ほうしょうきん}が{出|で}る。
examples.english: A reward is offered to anyone who provides useful information.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}は{優秀|ゆうしゅう}な{成績|せいせき}を{収|おさ}めた{社員|しゃいん}に{報奨金|ほうしょうきん}を{与|あた}える{制度|せいど}を{導入|どうにゅう}した。
examples.english: The company introduced a system of giving bonuses to employees who achieve outstanding results.

notes: Common collocations: {報奨金|ほうしょうきん}を{受|う}け{取|と}る (to receive a reward), {報奨金|ほうしょうきん}{制度|せいど} (incentive/reward system), {報奨金|ほうしょうきん}を{出|だ}す (to offer a reward). Used in various contexts: criminal investigations (reward for information), corporate incentives (performance bonuses), and government programs (incentive payments). Related: ボーナス (bonus — mainly for regular employment bonuses), {賞金|しょうきん} (prize money — for competitions), {懸賞金|けんしょうきん} (bounty — for wanted persons).
